videos.title: Beshear Demands Transparency on Sen. McConnell’s Health
videos.description:
Kentucky Democratic Governor Andy Beshear addressed concerns over Senator Mitch McConnell's prolonged absence from the Senate due to health issues. Governor Beshear revealed he sent letters to both McConnell and Senate Majority Leader John Thune requesting clear updates on McConnell's health and his ability to fulfill his senatorial duties. The conversation then turned to the upcoming midterms, with Beshear saying affordability will be the “driving issue.” He believes Democrats are speaking to voter’s “pain,” with people being unable to afford groceries, pharmaceuticals, and housing, forcing families to live paycheck to paycheck. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power."

videos.title: How Ukraine Is Stopping 90% of Russia's Drones (Exclusive) | WSJ
videos.description:
As Russia launches its largest aerial attacks of the war, overwhelming Ukrainian defenses with thousands of one-way attack drones and hundreds of advanced missiles, clearing the sky has become a key priority.

Four years into the war, Ukraine has developed its expertise in dealing with waves of Shahed-type drones, using machine guns, helicopters and electronic warfare to destroy them. Now, as Kyiv appeals to allies for Patriot interceptors to shoot down missiles, it’s leaning on cheap drones to defend cities from drone swarms.

WSJ got exclusive access to film the teams of pilots and navigators in the Lasar’s Group of the National Guard of Ukraine who are pivoting from attacks on Russian heavy equipment to hunting their drones.

videos.title: Helios Is AMD’s First AI System To Rival Nvidia Vera Rubin — We Got An Exclusive, First Look
videos.description:
AMD is one of the best performing chip stocks of 2026, following a decade-long comeback in data center chips. Now, it’s making its biggest competitive move against Nvidia yet. AMD’s first rack-scale system for AI, Helios, is shipping later this year - and it’s the world’s first competitor to Nvidia’s Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin systems. Now, Microsoft has signed up to use Helios in its data centers, joining other customers Meta, OpenAI and Oracle. But with a price tag of at least $5 million, analysts estimate Helios will cost at least $1 million more than Nvidia Vera Rubin. CNBC got an exclusive first look inside the 7,000 pound behemoth, and sat down with AMD data center and AI leads to ask how its first-generation AI system can compete with Nvidia - and what sets it apart.

videos.title: How Elon Musk's AI Empire In Memphis Became A Cautionary Tale
videos.description:
Elon Musk's xAI, now known as SpaceXAI following a merger with SpaceX, has made the Memphis, Tennessee area the center of its AI ambitions. XAI is building three data centers there, as well as a power plant in Southaven, Mississippi. XAI's AI infrastructure there truly deserves its name Colossus. It's a modern marvel that was built with breakneck speed. Anthropic and Google are now renting compute capacity at the data centers in a deals worth billions of dollars. But some say the buildout has been chaotic. XAI is now facing multiple lawsuits accusing the company of using loud, pollution-emitting gas turbines, some without the required Clean Air Act permits. CNBC traveled to Memphis and Southaven to speak with locals to learn why the data centers are such a flashpoint, to find out why backlash against data centers is spreading nationwide, and to learn what hyperscalers can do to win support as they race to build AI infrastructure.

videos.title: AI for Clean Air: Scaling Smarter Solutions
videos.description:
Air pollution is one of the most pressing development challenges globally, with far-reaching impacts on public health, economic growth, climate resilience, and sustainable development. In South Asia alone, nearly one billion people are exposed to hazardous air every day, leading to around one million premature deaths annually and shortening average life expectancy by more than three years.

This AI for Clean Air virtual event brought together global experts, innovators, and regional leaders to explore how artificial intelligence is transforming air quality management (AQM)—from real-time pollution mapping and predictive forecasting to private sector solutions and job creation.

Featuring perspectives from across South Asia and beyond, the discussion highlighted how AI-driven tools are moving from pilots to system-scale impact, showcased emerging partnerships, and examined policy pathways to scale solutions in complex and rapidly evolving environments.

Topics included artificial intelligence, air quality management, pollution forecasting, satellite monitoring, low-cost sensors, environmental governance, climate intelligence, public health, clean energy, and sustainable AI infrastructure.

Visit the event page: https://live.worldbank.org/en/event/2026/scaling-ai-solutions-to-tackle-air-pollution?cid=ECR_YT_worldbank_EN_EXT
